about: The statements of law, practice and fee that the application draft (stage 9) prints, each with its source and the date it was verified against that source. verified = null means not verified: the draft prints it with [M]. How to change this: a pull request to lib/trademark/filing/rules.json, with the source re-read on the day.

basis_1a.text: A use-based application states that the mark is in use in commerce, the date of first use anywhere, the date of first use in commerce, and includes one specimen per class.

basis_1b.text: An intent-to-use application is filed by a person with a bona fide intention, under circumstances showing good faith, to use the mark in commerce; the applicant verifies that intention.

declaration_1a.text: the signer believes the applicant to be the owner of the mark; the facts recited are accurate; the mark is in use in commerce; and to the best of the signer's knowledge no other person has the right to use the mark in commerce in a form likely to cause confusion.

declaration_1b.text: the signer believes the applicant to be entitled to use the mark in commerce; the applicant has a bona fide intention to use the mark in commerce; the facts recited are accurate; and to the best of the signer's knowledge no other person has the right to use the mark in commerce in a form likely to cause confusion.

declaration_false_statements.text: The TEAS declaration also warns that willful false statements are punishable; read the form's own text before signing.
declaration_false_statements.source: TEAS declaration text (not re-read for this build)

use_in_commerce_bona_fide.text: Use in commerce means the bona fide use of a mark in the ordinary course of trade, and not made merely to reserve a right in a mark.

use_in_commerce_goods.text: the mark is placed on the goods, their containers, the displays associated with them, or tags or labels affixed to them, and the goods are sold or transported in commerce

use_in_commerce_services.text: the mark is used or displayed in the sale or advertising of the services and the services are rendered in commerce

services_rendered_not_future.text: Use of a mark in the announcement of a future service, including an advance reservation or advance purchase, is not use as a service mark.

services_payment_not_required.text: Payment is not what makes a service: a service must be a real activity performed primarily for the benefit of others (free instructional events have been held a service).
services_payment_not_required.source: TMEP §§ 1301.01(a)(i)-(ii), 1301.01(b)(i) (May 2026); no express statement that payment is not required was found

feature_not_service.text: The name of a process, system, method or computer program is not a service mark unless it is also used to identify and distinguish a service.

specimen_required.text: A use-based application includes one specimen per class showing how the applicant uses the mark in commerce.

specimen_goods.text: A trademark specimen must show use of the mark on the goods, on containers or packaging, on labels or tags affixed to the goods, or on a display associated with the goods.

specimen_goods_webpage.text: A web page is a display associated with the goods when it shows the goods, shows the mark in association with them, and provides a means for ordering them.

service_mark_association.text: A service mark specimen must show the mark as used in the sale, rendering or advertising of the services, with a direct association between the mark and the services.

specimen_shows_mark_as_mark.text: The specimen must show the applied-for mark functioning as a mark for the goods or services identified.

specimen_webpage_url_date.text: A web page specimen must include its URL and the access or print date.

specimen_not_digitally_created.text: An artist's rendering, printer's proof, computer illustration, digital image or similar mockup, or an image digitally created or altered to include the mark, is not a proper specimen.

applicant_must_exist.text: The application must be filed by the party who owns the mark (or has the bona fide intention to use it) on the filing date; filed in the name of the wrong party it is void, and that cannot be cured by amendment or assignment. TMEP § 1201.02(c)(7) lets the name of a party that did not exist on the filing date be corrected in some cases; do not plan around it.

domicile.text: The applicant must give and keep current its domicile: the principal place of business of an entity, or a person's permanent legal residence. P.O. boxes, c/o, mail-receiving-agency, registered-agent and private-mailbox (PMB) addresses may be mailing addresses but are presumptively not domicile addresses. An applicant domiciled outside the United States must be represented by a qualified U.S. attorney.

itu_assignment_bar.text: An intent-to-use application cannot be assigned before an amendment to allege use or a statement of use is filed, except to a successor to the applicant's business, or the portion of it to which the mark pertains, if that business is ongoing and existing.

assignment_goodwill.text: A mark is assignable with the goodwill of the business in which it is used, or the part of the goodwill the mark symbolizes.

bona_fide_intent_evidence.text: Keep dated, objective evidence of the intention for each identification (business plans, product specifications, budgets, correspondence); an applicant without it is exposed to a lack-of-bona-fide-intent challenge (M.Z. Berger & Co. v. Swatch AG, 787 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2015)).
bona_fide_intent_evidence.source: M.Z. Berger & Co. v. Swatch AG, 787 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2015), as cited in the spec; not re-read for this build

free_form_surcharge.text: An identification not taken directly from the ID Manual carries the free-form text fee per class, plus a fee per class for each group of 1,000 characters beyond the first 1,000.

sou_deadline.text: After a notice of allowance, the statement of use is due within six months; extensions are granted in six-month increments, one plus up to four more, not more than 24 months in all beyond the first six.

office_action_response.text: An office action is answered within three months, with one optional three-month extension for a fee (a Madrid Section 66(a) application: six months, no extension).

fees.source: 37 C.F.R. § 2.6 (Cornell LII, through 89 FR 91089); uspto.gov/trademarks/trademark-fee-information (last updated Jan. 18, 2025)

excess_characters.label: Excess characters, each 1,000 beyond the first 1,000 (free-form)

allegation_of_use.label: Amendment to allege use or statement of use (electronic)

sou_extension.label: Extension of time to file a statement of use (electronic)
